title: P6 English (PSLE)
description: Primary 6 / PSLE English Paper 2, Language Use and Comprehension (MOE English Language Syllabus 2020; SEAB format from 2025): grammar, vocabulary, both cloze types, visual text, editing, synthesis and transformation, comprehension. A named routine for every component.
subject: english
syllabus: MOE English Language Syllabus 2020 (Primary); PSLE English Language 0001, format from 2025

archetypes.pattern: Tense from a time clue: past perfect with 'by the time', 'before', 'after'; present perfect with 'since', 'for', 'already'
Agreement with tricky subjects: neither/nor and either/or (nearer subject), each of, the number of, a pair of, uncountable nouns
Question tags after negative words (nobody, hardly, never), 'let's', 'I am' and indefinite pronouns
Conditionals: if + past perfect with would have; if + past with would; unless
Relative pronouns: who, whom, whose, which, where
Prepositions, connectors, modals, pronouns, gerund or infinitive, passive voice
Word from clues: contrast (although, but), cause (so, because) or a phrase that restates the blank
Phrasal verbs whose particle carries the meaning (call off, put up with, turn down)
Idioms and fixed expressions chosen from the situation
Nearest meaning of a word in a sentence
Vocabulary cloze: four options per blank, chosen from the paragraph's meaning and collocation
Main purpose or intended audience of a poster, flyer or web page
Conditions: age limits, item limits, deadlines, prices, what is free and what costs extra
Which statement is NOT true according to the visual text
Inference from layout, pictures or wording (who would be interested, why a detail is in bold)
Word-box grammar cloze: relatives, connectors, prepositions, pronouns, determiners; each word used once
Spelling: double letters, ie/ei, silent letters, suffix rules, frequently misspelled multisyllabic words
Grammar: tense, agreement, word form or preposition in a narrative passage
Function word from the sentence frame: preposition, connector, pronoun, helping verb, article
Content word from the passage's meaning (noun, verb, adjective) with one word only
Combine with a given word: despite, in spite of, although, unless, no sooner … than, not only … but also
Direct to reported speech (pronouns, tense, time and place words) and back
Active to passive voice, keeping the tense
Join with who, whom, whose, which or where
Find and state a fact from the passage
Inference: why, how do we know, what this shows about a character, what a remark means
Find a word or phrase in the passage that means …
What does a pronoun or 'one' refer to
Feeling with evidence lifted from the passage
True or false, with a reason from the passage
Order events or complete a flow of a character's feelings
